tasks.title: Write the structural checks over plugin/, each proven by a fixture it rejects
tasks.goal: Every later task is held to these checks: they keep the skills consistent with the command tree, the schemas, the on-disk layout and the embedded fence, and the eval cases in claude plugin eval's shape. They are Go tests in package cli (so they see NewRoot's command tree, the schema package and vloop.Fence), run over a plugin directory that defaults to plugin/ and can be pointed at a fixture copy with SKILLCHECK_PLUGIN_DIR — which is how the gate, and the close, plant defects in copies. On the base there are no skills yet, so the checks pass vacuously on the real plugin; that is expected.

references.why: P-2 to P-5, S-1 to S-3, B-5 and C-4: status is the driver's, gates exist before the work, sessions never commit, references are distributed not discovered, the language rule; and the "On disk" layout every .vloop/ path must come from

the driver's side of the contract: the prompts /vloop:<kind> <arg>, the handoff files .vloop/tmp/proposal.json and verdict.json, the fence's allowed and denied vloop commands, and that a dispute blocks the task with no attempt and no review
the behaviour contract, the worked example and the violations the review rules on

acceptance: internal/cli/skills_test.go defines TestPluginSkills, which runs every structural check over the plugin directory named by SKILLCHECK_PLUGIN_DIR, or ../../plugin when that variable is unset or empty, and reports each violation with t.Errorf naming the file or skill and the offending command, flag, schema, path, field or case
Frontmatter check: every plugin skills/<name>/SKILL.md has frontmatter name and description, and name equals <name>; a mismatch names the wrong name, a missing field names the field

Command-tree check: every `vloop <words> [--flags]` in a code span or fenced code block of any skill resolves to a command in NewRoot's tree, and every --flag it names exists on that command or as a global/persistent flag (so --json is accepted); `vloop` alone, `/vloop:work` and placeholders such as <id> are not violations

Schema check: every <name>/v<n> schema a skill names is in schema.Names(), and every fenced ```json block carrying a "schema" field validates against that schema with internal/schema's Validate; a block without a "schema" field is not checked

Path check: every .vloop/ path a skill names matches an entry of the "On disk" block of docs/domain/domain-model.md (placeholders such as <id> match one path segment); the check reads that block from the document, or holds a Go list that a test asserts equal to it

The "On disk" block of docs/domain/domain-model.md gains the .vloop/tmp/ entries as built by B6 — .vloop/tmp/proposal.json, .vloop/tmp/verdict.json, .vloop/tmp/plugin/<version>/ and .vloop/tmp/fence/<version>/settings.json — and .vloop/state/plan.md; no other line of the document changes

Skills-and-fence check: every vloop command in a code span or fenced block of the plan, work or review skill matches an allow rule of the embedded fence (vloop.Fence), and none matches a deny rule; the failure says "denied" for a denied command and "not allowed" for one the fence does not allow; the operate skill is exempt from this check but not from the command-tree check

Eval-format check: every plugin evals/<case>/ has a prompt.md whose frontmatter has max_turns and allowed_tools, and at least one graders/*.md whose frontmatter has type and weight; the failure names the case and the missing piece

TestSkillChecksRejectFixtures runs the checks over committed fixture plugins under internal/cli/testdata/skillcheck/ — at least one per check — and asserts each is rejected with a message naming the planted defect, and that a well-formed fixture is accepted
No check runs claude, reads this repository's .loop/ or .vloop/state/, or weakens an existing test

tasks.title: Port loop-plan to plugin/skills/plan as /vloop:plan, with the planner's three gate checks
tasks.goal: vloop run (B6) invokes /vloop:plan <brief path> and accepts whatever state/v1 plan it leaves; this skill is that session's whole instruction. It is the shell planner ported, not rewritten — the shell rules came from real runs — adapted to vloop's files and commands, plus the duties B2-B6 added: kind and area per task, references distributed from the brief only, the plan's prose in the configured language, and every gate executed on the base three ways before the plan is handed over (fails at a behavioural assertion, fixtures read back, matchers exercised against the pinned output). It also widens the embedded fence just enough for the commands a session is told to run.

references.why: the planner being ported — every rule (gate shapes, durable tests, regression net, naming, references with reasons) survives unless vloop's contracts change it, and a dropped rule needs its reason in the task notes
the plan the planner writes; run_id, brief and branch are the driver's to stamp, so the planner leaves them empty
the task fields the planner must fill (kind, area only when areas is set), the gate's rules and how a gate dispute blocks with no attempt charged

P-2 to P-5, S-1 to S-3, B-5 and C-4: status is the driver's, gates exist before the work, sessions never commit, references are distributed not discovered, the language rule; and the "On disk" layout every .vloop/ path must come from

acceptance: plugin/skills/plan/SKILL.md has frontmatter name: plan and a description; supporting files, if any, sit beside it in plugin/skills/plan/

It tells the session to write .vloop/state/state.json as state/v1 with base from `git rev-parse HEAD`, shell from `vloop config get shell`, status planning, iteration 0, created/updated timestamps, and run_id, brief and branch left as "" for the driver to stamp; and each task with id, title, goal, kind, files, references, depends_on, acceptance, verify, status pending, attempts 0, notes ""
It assigns kind to every task, and area only when `vloop config get areas` prints a value — then one of those values; never an area when areas is unset
References are the brief's binding references distributed to the tasks they bind, each with its reason; the skill forbids citing a document the brief does not cite (no discovery of references)

Before finishing it requires `vloop schema validate state/v1 .vloop/state/state.json` and `vloop task validate` to pass, and every task's gate to be run on the base with `vloop task gate <id>` and checked three ways: it fails on the base at a behavioural assertion; every fixture it builds is read back with commands that already exist; every matcher is exercised once against the exact output the brief pins — rewriting any gate that fails a check
It says a gate contradicting its own acceptance is left to the work session's gate_dispute, and that the planner's gates follow the plan's shell and the host's tools (BSD tools on macOS)
Titles, goals, acceptance criteria and notes are written in the language `vloop config get language` prints; keys, enum values, ids and commands stay English; the skill itself is English

Every rule of .claude/skills/loop-plan/SKILL.md survives, adapted to vloop (VLOOP_ACTIVE_TASK/VLOOP_GATE_TASK, .vloop/ paths), or its omission is explained in this task's notes; nothing tells the session to commit, set a status, move a ref, or run a command the fence denies
The skill carries at least one fenced json example with "schema": "state/v1" that validates and shows a fresh plan

fence/settings.json gains allow rules for exactly the vloop commands the skills tell sessions to run that it did not already allow (at least `vloop config get`, `vloop task validate`, `vloop task gate`); no deny rule is removed

tasks.goal: vloop run invokes /vloop:work <task id> and reads .vloop/tmp/proposal.json back as proposal/v1; a file that fails the schema counts as absent. This is the shell work skill ported to vloop's commands and files. The new duty is the dispute: when the gate cannot pass for a correct implementation, the session reports outcome blocked with a gate_dispute instead of bending the work or the gate — the driver then blocks the task at once with no attempt charged.

the driver's side of the contract: the prompts /vloop:<kind> <arg>, the handoff files .vloop/tmp/proposal.json and verdict.json, the fence's allowed and denied vloop commands, and that a dispute blocks the task with no attempt and no review
